After two night sessions, the French Parliament finally voted the Tardleu government’s tax reduction bill late this evening. Both houses then adjourned until June 3. The reductions provided by the bill, passed at 5 a.m. in the Chamber of Deputies after 24 hours of continuous debating, amounts to about $93,900,000. They affect chiefly taxes on stocks and bonds and financial transactions, the luxury taxes that have not been in force since the lean years of the franc, taxes on hotel bills and the business turnover tax on foodstuffs.
